column1: # Antibody CDR definitions -- the four numbering-scheme-relative loop ranges.
# PROVENANCE source http://www.bioinf.org.uk/abs/info.html "Antibody Information",
#              Prof. Andrew C. R. Martin's group, UCL -- the same group that
#              runs the abYsis server, which the 2017 ClusPro protocol names as
#              the way to identify CDRs for its own masking example
#              (Nat Protoc 12(2):255-278, published p.261, Step 8E(ii):
#              "To find CDRs... The resulting page provides three different
#              annotations of CDR regions (Chothia, ABM, and Kabat)").
#   retrieved  2026-08-13
#              (of the fetched HTML; the table below is transcribed from its
#              "CDR Definitions" section)
#   checked    Every row transcribed against the rendered table. The three
#              columns (kabat, abm, chothia) are the three
#              annotations the protocol says abYsis returns. The source table
#              also includes the contact and IMGT definitions.
#   status     [MEASURED] as a transcription. The ranges are in KABAT
#              NUMBERING (except where a row says otherwise), which is NOT the
#              numbering most PDB entries use -- see the warning below.
# WHY THERE ARE TWO H1 ROWS
#   The page gives CDR-H1 twice because the Kabat definition's end position is
#   spelled differently in the two numbering schemes: H35B under Kabat
#   numbering (which puts H1 insertions at 35A/35B) and H35 under
#   Chothia/Martin numbering (which puts them structurally). They denote the
#   same residues. `scheme` says which numbering each row is written in.
# THE WARNING, WHICH IS THE WHOLE REASON THIS FILE IS NOT ENOUGH ON ITS OWN
#   These ranges can only be applied to a chain that is *already* numbered in
#   the scheme named. Most deposited Fabs are not: 1FGN, the entry the ClusPro
#   protocol's own masking example uses, numbers both chains 1-214 sequentially
#   with no insertion codes at all. Indexing it with "L24-L34" happens to be
#   right and "H95-H102" is wrong by four residues, and nothing about the
#   arithmetic says which. `scripts/cdr.jl` therefore locates the loops by the
#   same page's conserved sequence anchors and ASSERTS each one, and uses this
#   table only for the part that is scheme-independent: which definitions exist
#   and hence what their union is.
# THE UNION, WHICH IS WHAT THE ANNOTATOR ACTUALLY NEEDS
#   The protocol masked "residues that were not considered to be in a CDR by
#   any of these annotations" (published p.273), i.e. it PRESERVED the union of
#   Kabat, AbM and Chothia. Reading the table down: Chothia is contained in AbM
#   for every loop and AbM is contained in Kabat for H2 while Kabat is
#   contained in AbM for H1, so
#       union = Kabat u AbM = L24-L34, L50-L56, L89-L97,
#   which is the `union` row below. It is DERIVED from the five transcribed
#   rows, not transcribed, and is marked so.
